title: Make Jig a stack-neutral monorepo control plane
description:
## Outcome

Jig becomes a stack-neutral monorepo control plane through authored repository contracts and one Jig-owned planning and execution model.

## Stack-Neutral Invariant

Components describe repository boundaries, actions describe commands, and profiles compose actions. Languages, frameworks, package managers, infrastructure tools, and application platforms are fixture inputs and leaf programs, never contract concepts. Supporting another stack must require authored configuration and ordinary command execution, not a Jig core feature or schema branch.

## Active Scope

Consolidate reusable setup for existing v6 acceptance behavior without centralizing feature-specific assertions, make adoption component authoring candidate-based and exclusion-aware, migrate this repository to v6, add a foreground repository action command over the existing execution service, and introduce only the string argument and literal argv authority required by concrete actions. Scale target freshness in a separate compatible contract epoch using the existing action input paths plus explicit completeness policy. Let dev apps optionally reuse serve-target launch authority after literal argv runners exist. Move LOC enforcement out of Jig-native Rust policy and into replaceable template-provided repository actions, proving that another ecosystem can use the same generic execution and evidence path without a core or schema branch.

## Adoption Boundary

Repository discovery proposes component candidates; it does not make every package manifest production authority. Adoption preview reports candidate roots, detection evidence, disposition, and explicit exclusions before write. Ambiguous candidates are not promoted by default. Discovery heuristics and exclusion inputs remain bootstrap concerns rather than runtime contract semantics; after adoption, authored components are authoritative.

## Dev Boundary

A dev app may reference a serve target to reuse argv, cwd, and base environment. Dev configuration remains authoritative for host, port, proxy, readiness, and session behavior. The existing dev supervisor remains the lifecycle owner; dev sessions do not become durable repository runs. Legacy inline dev configuration remains compatible.

## CI Boundary

A ci profile is an ordinary authored profile usable through the same CLI and MCP execution paths as any other profile. This epic does not generate or collapse repository CI workflows. Required-check names, job topology, service setup, matrices, migration base references, infrastructure jobs, and provider details remain repository-owned.

## Product Boundary

Reuse the existing repository catalog, planner, durable run model, receipts, gates, adapter descriptors, EvidenceReference DTOs, bootstrap inference/reporting, and dev supervisor. Do not introduce a second action graph, runtime language or framework model, Vite-specific contract semantics, adapter protocol, universal CI renderer, durable dev-run model, evidence vocabulary, cache, remote executor, or orchestration engine.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing v6 fixture construction is shared only where current behavior is genuinely common; feature-specific assertions remain with their owning tasks.
- Adoption previews candidate evidence and explicit exclusions; manifest presence alone does not author a component.
- Ambiguous or excluded candidates are not promoted, and authored components remain authoritative after adoption.
- Stack examples remain opaque components and commands; adding another ecosystem requires configuration rather than Jig core changes.
- Jig itself resolves as authored contract v6 with compatible developer workflows.
- Foreground CLI and MCP share the same planner and durable execution semantics.
- Dev apps may reuse serve-target argv, cwd, and base environment without transferring dev lifecycle ownership into durable runs.
- Legacy inline dev configuration remains compatible, and no Vite-specific contract semantics are added.
- Authored profiles, including ci, remain ordinary CLI and MCP inputs and do not generate workflow topology.
- The argument and runner epoch adds only proven string argument declarations, literal argv, and explicit compatibility shell authority.
- A separate freshness epoch uses ActionSpec.inputs as the sole path set plus explicit completeness policy and conservative fallback.
- No runtime language model, adapter protocol, universal CI renderer, generalized argument type system, second freshness path list, evidence store, artifact subsystem, multi-owner migration model, cache, remote execution, or delegated orchestrator is introduced.
- LOC enforcement is template-provided repository policy: Jig core has no native LOC semantics, Rust defaults remain replaceable or removable, and non-Rust equivalents use ordinary actions.
notes: Superseding architecture: feature .8 keeps closed .7 historically truthful while replacing the temporary per-repository Bash implementation with one language-neutral Jig file-budget capability. Repositories still own and may replace or remove the action and seed-once policy; Jig core owns generic measurement, comparison, typed execution, and evidence rather than Rust-specific LOC semantics.

title: Dogfood authored contracts and consolidate stack-neutral acceptance fixtures
description:
## Outcome

Jig dogfoods its current authored component, action, and profile contract while shared stack-neutral acceptance foundations remain grounded in the v6 behavior they actually support.

## Scope

Inventory existing v6 bootstrap/runtime fixtures and extract reusable construction or assertions only for behavior that already exists. Keep feature-specific ownership: exclusion-aware adoption remains .1.3, current-epoch source cutover and workflow preservation remain .1.2, and universal file-budget conformance remains under feature .8. Exercise materially different repository topologies through the same generic component, action, dependency, and profile semantics without turning ecosystem examples into contract concepts.

## Stack-neutral boundary

Languages, frameworks, package managers, infrastructure tools, mobile platforms, and desktop platforms remain opaque authored data. Adoption evidence does not become runtime semantics. Shared fixtures do not predeclare later contract epochs or absorb feature-specific assertions.
acceptance_criteria: Existing v6 fixture coverage is inventoried before shared setup changes; shared construction covers only genuinely common generic behavior; candidate/exclusion/write/recopy regressions remain .1.3; Jig source cutover and workflow preservation remain .1.2 against the epoch allocated when its dependencies land; universal file-budget tests remain feature .8 ownership; ecosystem examples stay opaque; existing compatibility coverage remains intact; focused tests plus freshly built JIG_DEV_BIN contract and test gates pass.

title: Extract shared stack-neutral v6 fixture foundations
description:
## Outcome

Existing v6 fixture construction and assertions share a small stack-neutral foundation without absorbing feature-specific acceptance ownership.

## Scope

Inventory the authored mixed-repository bootstrap fixture and the Go plus TypeScript runtime fixture. Record which existing coverage is retained, moved, removed, or intentionally distinct. Extract shared fixture construction and assertions only where current generic repository, component, action, dependency, profile, planning, affected-selection, command-backed execution, MCP, receipt, or gate behavior is already duplicated. Use replaceable topology scenarios only when the same assertion genuinely applies to both.

Candidate preview and exclusion behavior remains owned by `.1.3`; this repository's v6 cutover and workflow-preservation assertions remain owned by `.1.2`. This task must not implement those behaviors or prebuild dormant assertions for them.

## Boundaries

Use generic identifiers and lightweight command fixtures rather than real services or mandatory ecosystem toolchains. Do not create a permanent end-to-end mega-harness, anticipate new runner kinds, add adoption behavior, migrate this repository, or centralize feature-specific regression tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- An inventory names existing fixture coverage retained, moved, removed, or intentionally distinct.
- Shared fixture construction and assertions are extracted only for already-implemented generic contract and runtime behavior.
- The same shared assertions run against materially different topology scenarios without ecosystem-specific core branches.
- Candidate and exclusion behavior remains in .1.3; repository v6 cutover behavior remains in .1.2.
- No dormant future-feature assertions or permanent end-to-end mega-harness is introduced.
- Redundant builders and assertions are removed or explicitly justified, while legacy coverage remains passing and fixtures satisfy open-source hygiene.

title: Migrate Jig itself to the current authored contract epoch
description:
## Outcome

The Jig source tree dogfoods the authored repository, component, action, dependency, profile, alias, native-configuration, comparison, result, and evidence authority delivered by its completed dependencies.

## Scope

Allocate the then-current compatible contract epoch, cut .jig.toml and .agent/jig-contract.json to it, seed the repository-owned file-budget policy, author repo:file-budget in the default verification and CI/release paths, and preserve documented developer-facing checks. This task owns source dogfood exactly once; feature .8.6 only deletes the already-proven Bash implementation.

## Compatibility

Keep older supported contracts readable, coordinate epoch numbering with argv-runner work, treat checked-in source as authority, never hand-edit append-only state, and validate through a freshly built JIG_DEV_BIN.
acceptance_criteria: .jig.toml and .agent/jig-contract.json resolve reproducibly at the allocated authored epoch; repo:file-budget uses the seed-once policy, typed native configuration, target-local input semantics, durable comparison/result contract, and default profile; source CI and release validation invoke the universal action; existing info/check aliases, work gates, and documented developer workflows remain available or have explicit replacements; no Rust-native LOC dispatch is restored; cargo build -p jig-sh --bin jig followed by JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check contract and check test passes.
notes: Dependency rationale: source dogfood must consume the lifecycle-ready universal action from jig-sh-generic-monorepo-zac.8.5. It then proves the exact post-update authority required before jig-sh-generic-monorepo-zac.8.6 removes temporary Bash assets. Closed .7.2 remains historical context rather than the direct blocker.

title: Add exclusion-aware component candidate authoring to adoption
description:
## Outcome

Adoption proposes reviewable component candidates and requires explicit inclusion or exclusion decisions where repository evidence is ambiguous, so incidental package manifests do not become production components.

## Evidence

Inspected non-Jig repositories contain plausible Cargo and JavaScript package manifests beneath mocks, experiments, videos, marketing sites, and support tools. Raw manifest presence is therefore insufficient production-component authority.

## Scope

Extend the existing bounded, Git-aware adoption scan and inference report rather than adding a second discovery engine. Emit deterministic component candidates with repository-relative root, proposed identity, detection signals and sources, confidence, and disposition: included, explicitly excluded, or review required. Accept adoption-only exact-root exclusions through interactive or noninteractive answer inputs and show their effect in human and JSON previews. Begin with exact roots; do not introduce a general glob or ignore language without further evidence.

Existing workspace membership, explicit answers, and high-confidence repository structure may justify inclusion. A standalone manifest hit alone does not: ambiguous candidates remain visible as review required and are not authored by default. An adoption write authors only accepted candidates. Exclusion inputs and detection heuristics remain at the bootstrap boundary and do not become runtime component, affected-ignore, planner, or execution semantics. Once adopted, checked-in authored components remain authoritative for update or recopy. This task owns its candidate, exclusion, write, and recopy regression assertions.

## Compatibility

Preserve existing explicit component answers and supported high-confidence adoption behavior. Existing repositories without exclusion inputs continue to preview safely; ambiguous newly visible candidates are reported rather than silently promoted.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adoption preview deterministically reports candidate root, proposed identity, evidence, confidence, disposition, and reason in human and JSON output.
- Adoption-only exact-root exclusions are explicit and validated.
- A raw Cargo.toml or package.json hit is insufficient to author a component.
- Ambiguous and excluded candidates remain visible but are not promoted by default.
- Writes consume the reviewed decisions, while update and recopy preserve authored components without rediscovery.
- Existing bounded Git-aware scan and inference metadata are reused.
- Exclusions do not become runtime contract, planner, affected-ignore, or execution semantics.
- Generic fixtures cover production and incidental manifest trees without private identifiers.

title: Add a generic repository action execution surface
description:
## Outcome

Humans, agents, and automation execute authored repository actions through one Jig-owned planner, safety model, foreground CLI, MCP surface, and durable runtime.

## Scope

Add `jig run` over the existing execution service. Replace the migration-specific argument wire shape with the minimum declared string argument semantics required by the current migration-add action. Then activate a dedicated runner contract epoch for literal direct argv and explicit compatibility shell execution. Preserve effects, approvals, source identity, leases, cancellation, deterministic plans, target results, receipts, and legacy command-backed v6 repositories.

Target freshness is not part of this contract epoch; feature `.4` owns a separate compatible freshness epoch and does not block the foreground execution surface.

## Product Boundary

Jig owns selection, planning, dependency layers, execution, and result accounting. Ecosystem programs are declared leaf implementations. No caller-provided shell, generalized argument type system, freshness schema, cache, remote execution, dev-session ownership, or artifact policy is included.
acceptance_criteria:
- jig run and MCP share planning, safety, durable execution, and target results.
- Only named string arguments required by concrete actions are declared and normalized into plan identity.
- Migration-add uses the declared argument mechanism without waiting for an argv runner.
- A dedicated runner epoch distinguishes literal argv from explicit compatibility shell execution and binds only already-declared arguments.
- Freshness authority remains in feature .4 and does not block foreground execution.
- Legacy v6 command runners remain compatible.

title: Add foreground jig run over the shared repository execution service
description:
## Outcome

A human-facing foreground `jig run` command executes repository plans through the same Jig-owned service used by MCP, without duplicating transport logic or delegating orchestration.

## Scope

Extract a transport-neutral Jig execution service and add selectors, profiles, affected mode, explain, plan IDs, fail-fast, JSON output, cancellation, status, and exact repeated effect approvals.
acceptance_criteria:
- Equivalent CLI and MCP requests produce the same RunPlan and durable target results and receipts.
- Explain creates no run, lease, or effect approval.
- Effectful execution requires explicit selectors and exact --approve-effect worktree/external flags; there is no broad --yes bypass.
- Foreground cancellation cleans up Jig-owned child processes and leaves a truthful terminal run state.
- Repository dependency layers and target result accounting remain owned by Jig.
- Pre-v6 repositories receive an actionable migration diagnostic.

title: Declare minimal string action arguments and binding semantics
description:
## Outcome

Actions declare the smallest deterministic parameter surface required by current repository operations.

## Scope

Replace the migration-specific wire shape with named string argument declarations on `ActionSpec`, required and optional presence, conservative length validation, target-qualified CLI and MCP binding, and deterministic plan hashing. Migrate the existing migration-add name authority to this declared mechanism, including its Jig-native runner binding.

Direct argv runner discriminants and literal argv binding positions are owned by `.3.3`; this task must not implement or specify freshness authority.

## Boundaries

Do not add boolean, integer, choice, JSON, secret, arbitrary command, variadic, shell-interpolated, or freshness arguments. Add another type only with a named action that cannot be represented safely as a string.
acceptance_criteria:
- Named string arguments are declared on ActionSpec and validated consistently across source, resolved contract, CLI, MCP, planning, and Jig-native execution.
- Unknown, missing, duplicate, empty when forbidden, oversized, and unselected-target arguments fail before plan creation.
- Normalized values participate in deterministic plan identity.
- Migration-add name authority uses the declared mechanism and legacy no-argument actions remain unchanged.
- Direct argv runner kinds and binding positions remain owned by .3.3.
- No additional argument types or freshness fields are introduced.

title: Activate an argv and explicit-shell contract epoch
description:
## Outcome

A dedicated repository-contract epoch activates literal direct-argv execution and explicit compatibility shell authority while reusing the declared string argument semantics from `.3.2`.

## Scope

Add argv and shell runner discriminants, declare literal binding positions for already-declared string arguments, and migrate generated sources to the new runner epoch. Retain v6 command-key compatibility and ensure older runtimes cannot silently select the new schema. This task owns runner execution, binding, source and resolved schema migration, and runner-choice recopy compatibility; it does not add a second argument declaration mechanism.

Freshness authority belongs to feature `.4` and its separate compatible contract epoch.

## Product Boundary

Every runner is a leaf implementation inside a Jig-owned plan. Runner configuration cannot supply a competing graph, schedule, result lifecycle, cache, freshness claim, or remote executor.
acceptance_criteria:
- Literal argv execution never passes programs, fixed arguments, or bound declared values through shell parsing.
- Explicit shell runners accept no argument interpolation.
- Runner binding reuses the declarations and validation introduced by .3.2 rather than creating a second argument mechanism.
- The runner epoch preserves Jig planning, effects, approvals, source validation, cancellation, durable state, and target results.
- v6 command-key sources and resolved contracts remain readable, and recopy preserves authored runner choice.
- No freshness schema, additional argument types, output declarations, caching, remote execution, or delegated runner protocol is introduced.

title: Specify delegated-runner v1 and execution-unit planning
description:
## Outcome

Batch-capable external execution engines integrate through a neutral protocol and an explicit plan model rather than engine-specific branches.

## Scope

Define versioned DTO/schema, DelegateSpec authority, opaque project identity, execution units/batches, request/result accounting, and interactions with effects, leases, source epochs, arguments, and evidence references.

## Acceptance Criteria

- RunPlan represents execution units without losing target-level dependency and result identity.
- Protocol requests contain only validated authority and selected targets; responses must account exactly once for every requested unit/target.
- Unknown versions, extra/missing/duplicate results, invalid status transitions, and authority mismatches fail closed.
- The design reserves evidence/log/artifact references and does not require a core change for each external engine.
- Schema/example compatibility tests are committed.
acceptance_criteria:
- RunPlan represents execution units without losing target-level dependency and result identity.
- Protocol requests contain only validated authority and selected targets; responses must account exactly once for every requested unit/target.
- Unknown versions, extra/missing/duplicate results, invalid status transitions, and authority mismatches fail closed.
- The design reserves evidence/log/artifact references and does not require a core change for each external engine.
- Schema/example compatibility tests are committed.
delete_reason: Removed from the epic: competing monorepo-engine delegation is outside Jig native execution scope.

title: Implement delegated-runner supervision and a generic batch fixture
description:
## Outcome

Jig safely executes delegated units while retaining ownership of planning, source validation, effects, leases, cancellation, durable state, and receipts.

## Scope

Implement bounded direct-argv supervision, deterministic layer scheduling, unioned lease acquisition, source checks, exact result ingestion, cleanup, and a generic fixture bridge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Timeout, cancellation, output overflow, child-tree cleanup, malformed/partial response, and source drift yield truthful deterministic failures.
- Jig—not the delegate—owns effect approval, lease authority, run lifecycle, and receipt persistence.
- Batch and per-target units honor dependency layers and produce stable target result ordering.
- A generic fixture demonstrates integration without naming or branching on a specific build engine.
- CLI and MCP observe the same delegated run state.
acceptance_criteria:
- Timeout, cancellation, output overflow, child-tree cleanup, malformed/partial response, and source drift yield truthful deterministic failures.
- Jig—not the delegate—owns effect approval, lease authority, run lifecycle, and receipt persistence.
- Batch and per-target units honor dependency layers and produce stable target result ordering.
- A generic fixture demonstrates integration without naming or branching on a specific build engine.
- CLI and MCP observe the same delegated run state.
delete_reason: Removed from the epic: Jig owns native monorepo planning and execution; no delegated-runner implementation.

title: Scale target evidence freshness by declared authority
description:
## Outcome

Unrelated monorepo changes no longer invalidate target evidence when a target explicitly declares its existing action inputs complete for freshness, while plans and running actions retain whole-repository staleness and mutation safety.

## Scope

Introduce a versioned freshness policy that marks the existing `ActionSpec.inputs` path set as exhaustive. Absence of that policy retains repository-wide conservative freshness. Do not add a parallel `freshness_inputs` list. Define transitive dependency and runner authority, establish a reproducible baseline on an anonymized large-repository fixture, activate a separate compatible freshness contract epoch, compute correct target-scoped identities, and cut new receipts and gates over with conservative legacy fallback. Reuse source observation across targets when straightforward. Add batching or other performance machinery only when measurements demonstrate material repeated-walk cost.

## Product Boundary

Jig computes freshness only from checked-in contracts and its own executions. Missing completeness policy, ambiguous, failed, unsupported, or excessive authority is unknown or stale, never fresh.

## Not In Scope

A second path-authority list, persistent full logs, content-addressed evidence storage, declared output or artifact manifests, archival lifecycle, cache reuse, remote stores, execution skipping, remote execution, elaborate symlink or submodule projection, and a dedicated performance service are not part of this feature.
acceptance_criteria:
- A versioned policy marks the existing ActionSpec.inputs set exhaustive for freshness; no parallel freshness_inputs list is added.
- Missing completeness policy retains repository-wide conservative freshness.
- A reproducible baseline demonstrates unrelated-change invalidation and records source-observation behavior.
- Complete scoped declarations ignore unrelated paths and invalidate on direct inputs, transitive dependencies, or runner authority.
- Missing, failed, ambiguous, or unsupported authority never reports fresh.
- Whole-repository plan and mutation safety remains unchanged.
- Legacy journals remain readable without false freshness.
- Correct target-scoped identities are implemented before performance machinery, and further optimization requires measured repeated-walk cost.

title: Specify conservative freshness policy over canonical action inputs
description:
## Outcome

An implementation-ready contract design distinguishes affected-selection hints from exhaustive target freshness authority without duplicating path declarations.

## Scope

Specify a versioned freshness policy that can mark the existing `ActionSpec.inputs` path set exhaustive. Policy absence retains repository-wide conservative freshness. Define transitive action authority, command and Jig-native runner authority contributions, digest domains, typed `TargetFreshness` states, and compatibility requirements for old plans, runs, receipts, and append-only journals.

This task owns the semantics and compatibility design only. It must not introduce `freshness_inputs`, implement fingerprint collection, migrate plan or journal schemas, or cut gates over; `.4.2` and `.4.3` own those implementation steps.
acceptance_criteria:
- ActionSpec.inputs remains the sole declared path set for both affected selection and freshness evaluation.
- A versioned explicit policy marks that path set exhaustive; policy absence remains repository-wide conservative.
- The design covers transitive action dependencies and selected runner authority in a versioned digest domain.
- Typed freshness states fail conservatively for unknown, unsupported, ambiguous, or failed authority.
- Compatibility requirements ensure old plans, runs, receipts, and journals remain readable without gaining false freshness.
- No freshness_inputs field, fingerprint implementation, plan or journal migration, or gate cutover is introduced by this specification task.

title: Implement correct target source and authority fingerprints
description:
## Outcome

The separate freshness contract epoch and evidence collection compute correct deterministic target-scoped identities without committing to unsupported filesystem projection or premature performance architecture.

## Entry Evidence

Before optimizing collection, add a reproducible anonymized repository fixture of roughly 4,000 files that demonstrates unrelated-change invalidation and records source-observation counts or elapsed instrumentation as target counts increase. Use the baseline only to decide whether repeated repository walks are materially costly.

## First Implementation

- Activate the freshness policy specified by `.4.1` while keeping `ActionSpec.inputs` as the sole path declaration.
- Add versioned plan identity and additive journal metadata required for scoped freshness; preserve deserialization of old plans, runs, and receipts without granting false freshness.
- Compute correct target-scoped identities from declared-complete inputs, transitive dependencies, and runner authority.
- Share a source projection or observation across targets when straightforward within the existing architecture.
- Fail conservatively when filesystem authority is unsupported, ambiguous, escaping, or cannot be collected.
- Add batching, indexing, caching, or a dedicated performance service only when the anonymized baseline demonstrates material repeated-walk cost.

## Scope Boundary

The inspected repository corpus contains no tracked symlinks or submodules. Do not build elaborate symlink or submodule projection logic. Minimal detection that returns unknown or blocked is sufficient. Do not make performance architecture a prerequisite for correctness.
acceptance_criteria:
- The separate freshness epoch uses ActionSpec.inputs plus the completeness policy from .4.1 and introduces no second path list.
- Versioned plan identity and additive journal metadata remain compatible with old plans, runs, and receipts without granting false freshness.
- Correct target-scoped fingerprints are deterministic across target ordering.
- Relevant direct inputs, transitive dependencies, and runner authority invalidate freshness while unrelated changes do not.
- Missing policy or unsupported, ambiguous, escaping, or failed authority returns unknown or blocked rather than fresh.
- Correctness does not depend on batching, indexing, caching, or a dedicated performance service.
- Source observation is shared when straightforward; further optimization requires anonymized roughly 4,000-file measurements demonstrating material repeated-walk cost.
- No elaborate symlink or submodule projection logic is introduced.

title: Cut receipts and gates over to scoped target freshness
description:
## Outcome

New receipts and gate evaluation use target-scoped freshness while preserving global execution safety and legacy journal compatibility.

## Scope

Populate additive freshness metadata, update target evidence evaluation, keep whole-repository source identity in plans/runs, and retain the one-complete-run profile gate rule.
acceptance_criteria:
- A plan created before any repository source change remains globally stale and cannot execute.
- A read-only action mutating any non-.agent path fails even outside its freshness inputs.
- New target receipts evaluate scoped freshness; legacy receipts use legacy rules and never gain false freshness.
- Profile gates still require all targets from one complete successful run.
- Diagnostics explain whether source inputs, dependency authority, runner authority, legacy schema, or collection failure caused staleness.

title: Let dev apps reuse serve-target launch authority
description:
## Outcome

A dev app can reference an authored serve target instead of duplicating launch command authority, while the existing dev supervisor retains all session semantics.

## Evidence

The inspected Jig configurations repeat every frontend identity and directory in dev configuration: one frontend across two dev apps, three across five, and five across six. This task removes that demonstrated authority duplication without generalizing dev sessions into repository runs.

## Scope

Add an optional serve-target reference to dev app source and resolved configuration. When present, resolve argv, cwd, and base environment from the referenced target. Keep host, port, proxy, readiness, restart, process supervision, and other session behavior in dev configuration. Define deterministic environment composition so dev-session values can augment the target base without creating a second base-command authority. Preserve update or recopy behavior and diagnostics for missing, incompatible, or conflicting references.

## Compatibility

Legacy inline dev app command, directory, and environment configuration remains readable and behaves unchanged. Repositories may migrate one dev app at a time.

## Product Boundary

The target reference reuses launch authority only. The existing dev supervisor launches and owns the process. Starting or stopping a dev session does not create a RunPlan, durable repository run, target result, receipt, or gate evidence. Do not add Vite, React, Node, Rust, Go, Electron, or other ecosystem-specific fields or inference to the repository contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- Optional serve-target references reuse target-owned argv, cwd, and base environment.
- Dev configuration remains authoritative for host, port, proxy, readiness, restart, and session lifecycle.
- Conflicting or invalid authority fails precisely before launch.
- Legacy inline and target-backed dev apps coexist and preserve existing inline behavior.
- Recopy preserves authored references and does not infer them.
- Dev sessions remain supervisor-owned and create no durable run, target result, receipt, or gate evidence.
- No Vite-specific or other ecosystem-specific contract semantics are introduced.

title: Make LOC enforcement a template-owned repository action
description:
## Outcome

LOC limits become repository quality policy rather than Jig product policy. Rust templates still provide the existing LOC check by default, but the check is an ordinary command-backed repository action with the same planning, supervision, gate, and receipt behavior available to any language.

## Product Decision

Jig owns action selection, affected planning, dependency ordering, execution supervision, result parsing, durable evidence, and gates. A repository owns which files count as source, how lines are counted, thresholds, generated-file handling, exceptions, and legacy grandfathering. LOC does not protect a Jig correctness, security, persistence, or compatibility invariant, so it does not justify a native runtime branch.

A template may provide opinionated defaults. That is template policy, not a contract concept: repositories may replace or remove the action, and another language may add its own command-backed LOC action without changing Jig core. Repository ownership includes lifecycle authority: update and recopy must preserve an authored replacement, removal, alias choice, and profile membership instead of silently restoring the template default.

## Scope

First make the managed Rust checker self-contained while preserving the behavior currently implemented by `jig check rust-file-loc`. Then remove the dedicated CLI, command DTOs, dispatch, policy implementation, and native tests. Keep the generated Rust action and optional `jig.rust_file_loc` compatibility alias as ordinary declared command authority only. Route v6 automation through the resolved action/profile and prove an authored non-Rust LOC action uses the same generic execution and evidence path.

Update current source dogfooding, release/fixture invocations, documentation, managed templates, embedded snapshots, and contract compatibility coverage. Receipt and evidence updates apply to newly emitted records through the generic action path; historical `.agent/state/*.jsonl` remains truthful append-only memory and must not be rewritten. The existing Jig contract-v6 migration must consume this boundary rather than preserving the historical native policy.

## Compatibility

Perform the cutover in dependency order: publish the self-contained managed checker before deleting native behavior. Generated repositories are source-revision pinned, so historical repositories continue using the runtime matching their historical wrapper; update/recopy publishes the new checker and binding together. The current runtime must still load supported older contracts and execute LOC when it is declared as an ordinary command-backed tool. Do not retain native LOC semantics solely as an undocumented fallback for obsolete wrapper contents.

## Non-Goals

Do not introduce a generic LOC schema, threshold DSL, `FileLocPolicy` runtime type, language registry branch, native cross-language checker, mandatory TypeScript policy, new action runner, second planner, or new evidence format. Do not change the generic action-execution design owned by the repository-action feature.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fresh Rust templates include their LOC policy as an ordinary command-backed repository action in the default verification profile.
- Jig core exposes no native Rust LOC policy implementation or dedicated Rust LOC command semantics.
- The current Rust thresholds, baseline behavior, and exception rules remain available through the template-owned checker.
- A non-Rust component can author and run an equivalent LOC action without a Jig schema, registry, CLI, or runtime change.
- Supported older contract shapes continue to execute a declared LOC command tool without native dispatch.
- CI, docs, generated snapshots, and newly emitted work evidence and receipts reflect the repository-action ownership boundary; historical append-only state is not rewritten.
- No generic LOC DSL, native cross-language LOC engine, universal thresholds, or TypeScript LOC default is introduced.
- After a repository replaces or removes the template LOC action, compatibility alias, or default-profile membership, update and recopy preserve that authored authority and do not recreate omitted defaults.

title: Make the managed Rust LOC checker self-contained
description:
## Outcome

The managed Rust LOC checker becomes the complete implementation of the Rust template's opinionated source-size policy. It no longer delegates policy to Jig core, so it can serve as the command implementation behind an ordinary repository action and legacy command alias.

## Why This Comes First

Deleting native policy before publishing a replacement would break the current source repository, generated CI, release validation, rendered-repository fixtures, and older command-backed contracts. This task establishes behavioral equivalence at the repository boundary before the runtime surface is removed.

## Scope

Move the characterized behavior from `crates/jig/src/policy.rs` into the managed checker source and its embedded snapshot. Preserve the current physical-line semantics and thresholds: information above 400, soft warnings above 500 and 600, hard failure above 800, and absolute failure above 1000. Preserve non-increasing legacy files above hard or absolute thresholds, rename-aware previous counts, `agentic-loc-exception:` and `@generated` markers within the first 40 lines, and the distinction between errors, warnings, and informational output.

Give the checker a direct, testable invocation contract covering the generated positional default-branch form plus `--changed-against REF`, `--staged`, and `--all`. Exactly one mode is effective. The default-branch form resolves the remote merge base when available and retains the documented local/empty-tree fallbacks. Use NUL-delimited Git authority throughout candidate and rename discovery; do not regress paths merely because shell implementation is convenient.

Keep this implementation Rust-template-specific: Rust roots, `*.rs`, thresholds, and annotations belong in the checker. Do not create Jig configuration fields or a reusable cross-language LOC library. The generated contract-v6 `rust-file-loc` action continues to point at this command, and the current source repository can continue declaring `jig.rust_file_loc` as a command-backed compatibility tool.

## Validation Ownership

Add focused checker tests for every mode and policy band, new and deleted files, renamed oversized legacy files, annotated and generated files, invalid mode combinations, missing refs, and unusual valid filenames. Update rendered-repository smoke coverage to demonstrate the checker runs without native LOC support. Keep fixtures unmistakably generic.

## Root And Counting Compatibility

Preserve the configured Rust source-root authority currently supplied by `rust_crate_roots`; do not silently hard-code `crates`. The managed template must safely represent zero, one, or multiple valid repository-relative roots, including `.`. To preserve current Git pathspec behavior, zero configured roots means repository-wide Rust candidate selection rather than an empty candidate set. Update or recopy must refresh generated default root authority without overriding a repository-authored replacement action.

Match the current line-count boundary exactly: an empty file has zero lines, each non-empty final segment counts even without a trailing newline, and LF or CRLF line endings produce the same line count. Validate these cases at the exact 400, 500, 600, 800, and 1000 boundaries so a shell implementation cannot substitute newline counting with different behavior.

## Shell Portability

The managed checker must run on the stock macOS Bash 3.2 surface as well as supported newer Bash versions. Do not use associative arrays, `mapfile` or `readarray`, empty-array expansions that fail under `set -u`, or other post-3.2 syntax. Preserve NUL-delimited Git parsing with Bash 3.2-compatible primitives and cover the generated script with a macOS or equivalent Bash 3.2 portability smoke test.
acceptance_criteria:
- The managed checker performs LOC enforcement without invoking a native `jig check rust-file-loc` implementation.
- Positional default-branch, `--changed-against`, `--staged`, and `--all` modes have one documented, fail-closed selection contract.
- The existing 400/500/600/800/1000 informational, soft, hard, and absolute thresholds are preserved.
- Legacy non-growth above hard/absolute limits, rename baselines, first-40-line exception markers, generated markers, deletions, and new files retain characterized behavior.
- Candidate and rename handling is safe for valid Git path bytes supported by the existing harness, including whitespace and line breaks, and does not parse line-delimited Git filenames.
- Errors produce nonzero status; warnings and informational findings remain successful and identify the affected repository-relative file.
- The managed template source and embedded snapshot stay identical, and focused tests cover every policy branch and invocation mode.
- The checker uses only dependencies guaranteed by supported generated Rust repositories on Linux and macOS.
- The generated checker preserves configured Rust source-root authority without hard-coding `crates`: zero roots retain repository-wide Rust candidate selection, while one or multiple valid roots, including `.`, constrain Git pathspecs as today; focused tests cover each case plus update or recopy refresh.
- Line counting preserves the characterized empty-file, LF, CRLF, trailing-newline, and unterminated-final-line behavior at every exact threshold boundary.
- The generated checker executes on stock macOS Bash 3.2 and supported newer Bash versions without post-3.2 syntax; portability coverage exercises NUL-delimited candidates and the zero-root case under `set -u`.

title: Remove native Rust LOC policy and use repository actions end to end
description:
## Outcome

Jig runtime and CLI no longer know how to count Rust lines or enforce Rust-specific size policy. Every active LOC check, including the Rust template default, executes as repository-declared command authority through the ordinary contract-v6 action path.

## Dependency

This task begins only after the managed checker is self-contained and behaviorally characterized. The deletion must not create a window where generated repositories or the Jig source tree have no functioning LOC gate.

## Core Removal

Delete the dedicated `rust-file-loc` Clap subcommand and options, command/request/input DTOs, conversion and runtime dispatch arms, `PolicyCheckCommand` branch, compiled LOC constants and implementation, Rust-only candidate/rename helpers that become unused, CLI/tool-definition constants, moved-command hints, and native policy unit tests. Remove the name from strict launcher subcommand metadata so contract-v6 parsing can treat `rust-file-loc` as an external action selector.

Do not replace the removed code with a generic native LOC abstraction. The ordinary action runner, input globs, profiles, result parsing, receipts, and work evidence are the complete Jig product surface.

## End-to-End Cutover

Update source and generated command bindings, release validation, rendered-repository scripts, workflow templates, bootstrap previews, help text, documentation, and embedded snapshots. On contract v6, `jig check rust-file-loc` is selector syntax for the authored action; it is no longer a special command and accepts no LOC-specific flags. Direct policy-mode validation uses `scripts/check-rust-file-loc.sh`.

Generated v6 repository-policy CI should invoke the resolved selector or verification profile so the template default exercises the same action path as any custom language check. During the source repository's pre-v6 interval, its declared `jig.rust_file_loc` command tool may continue to call the self-contained checker; the existing v6 dogfood bead will complete that source cutover after this task.

## Compatibility

Keep supported contract epochs readable and keep normal command-backed tool execution intact. An alias named `jig.rust_file_loc` may remain in a generated or authored manifest, but it is data: the runtime resolves its command like any other alias. Add coverage for a supported older contract whose LOC command is self-contained and verify there is no recursion or native fallback. Historical generated repositories remain bound to their configured source revision; update/recopy publishes the new managed checker before a repository moves to the source revision containing this deletion. For an authored contract-v6 repository, recopy must preserve an exact replacement or removal of the LOC action, its compatibility alias, and its profile membership; template defaults apply only while the generated model remains unmodified.

## Stack-Neutral Proof

Add a lightweight contract-v6 fixture with a non-Rust component, ordinary source files, and a repository-authored `file-loc` command action. Prove exact and action-wide selector resolution, affected input selection, supervised failure, and newly emitted receipts and required evidence use the generic machinery without a language registry edit. Preserve historical append-only receipts and journals unchanged. The fixture checker may be deliberately small; it proves ownership and execution parity, not a TypeScript policy recommendation.

## Documentation Boundary

Document LOC as an example of template-provided repository policy. State that templates may provide defaults, repositories own semantics, and new languages add ordinary actions. Remove statements classifying Rust LOC as runtime-owned or native. Keep fixture identifiers generic and do not introduce downstream project details.
acceptance_criteria:
- `CheckRustFileLocOpts`, `RustFileLocRequest`, `RustFileLocInput`, native dispatch variants, compiled thresholds, Rust candidate helpers, and dedicated policy tests are absent from Jig core.
- Contract v6 resolves `jig check rust-file-loc` as the ordinary authored action selector; LOC-specific mode flags belong only to the checker command.
- Generated v6 CI and work verification execute the resolved Rust LOC action/profile instead of bypassing it or invoking native policy.
- `jig.rust_file_loc`, when retained for compatibility, is only a manifest-declared command alias and has no feature-registry or native runtime semantics.
- Supported pre-v6 contract fixtures execute a self-contained command-backed LOC tool without recursion or native fallback.
- An authored non-Rust component LOC action participates in selection, affected planning, supervision, receipts, and evidence using only existing generic contracts.
- Help, launcher metadata, docs, release checks, fixture scripts, embedded snapshots, and generated workflows contain no stale native-LOC instructions.
- Focused tests plus `cargo test -p jig-sh` and a freshly built `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test` pass.
- No generic LOC engine, LOC schema, threshold configuration, or TypeScript LOC default is added.
- Recopy and update coverage proves that authored replacement or removal of the LOC action, `jig.rust_file_loc` alias, and verification-profile membership survives without regeneration of omitted defaults.
- Newly emitted LOC receipts and work evidence identify the generic repository action path, while existing `.agent/state/*.jsonl` history remains unchanged and readable.

title: Make file budgets a universal repository capability
description:
## Outcome

Jig supplies one language-neutral reviewability-budget engine while each repository owns strict checked-in policy. Physical lines and exact bytes use a per-metric no-growth debt ratchet across explicit Git comparison authority.

## Architecture

A pure evaluator and canonical Git comparison service feed a durable native-action contract, direct CLI and CI, seed-once repository lifecycle, source dogfood, and final removal of the temporary Bash checker. The native default remains replaceable or removable.

## Superseding decision

This feature preserves the repository-action boundary delivered by closed feature .7 while superseding its former no-generic-engine non-goal. Closed history remains unchanged. The full reviewed architecture is in docs/plans/universal-file-budget.md.
acceptance_criteria: Jig has one dependency-free language-neutral file-budget engine; repositories own a versioned seed-once policy; lines and bytes ratchet independently; renames preserve ancestry and copies are new; exact bounded expiring waivers cannot be laundered; comparison, findings, receipts, time validity, and crash recovery are deterministic; no AST registry, external LOC binary, baseline ledger, second runner, or second evidence store is introduced; the temporary Bash checker is deleted only after source dogfood proves the universal action.

title: Implement the versioned file-budget policy and pure evaluator
description:
## Outcome

Add an internal jig-file-budget workspace crate that parses strict version 1 policy, measures supplied byte streams, and evaluates line and byte debt without Git, CLI, process, repository-state, or jig-contract ownership.

## Boundary

Own policy DTOs, disjoint glob rules, display categories, reasoned exclusions, stable exact waiver IDs, ceiling and expiry validation, raw and semantic policy identity inputs, physical LF lines, exact bytes, independent debt coordinates, authorization continuity, and deterministic pure diagnostics. Do not own comparison resolution, action execution, templates, or evidence journals.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown fields, invalid cardinality or numeric bounds, protected authority paths, ambiguous rules, malformed or expired waivers, and waiver removal with debt fail deterministically; line and byte counting is byte-oriented and streaming; debt cannot grow under unchanged ordinary policy without an active bounded waiver; policy and comparison facts are supplied explicitly; pure/table/property tests prove syntax neutrality across common source-language paths without invoking language toolchains.

title: Extract canonical Git comparison, scope, and target matching primitives
description:
## Outcome

Extract one bounded comparison and rename-preserving scope service from existing git_receipts internals, plus a target-local matcher primitive for non-empty action inputs.

## Boundary

Own merge-base, exact-tree, index-against-HEAD, strict-inventory, and unborn-worktree comparison mechanics; requested, peeled-commit, and tree identities; worktree/index/inventory views; untracked inclusion; rename ancestry; copy-as-new; completeness; flattened affected paths; pinned Git safety; and the matcher primitive. Do not publish an external scope protocol, persist unbounded entry lists, or activate new-epoch semantics by itself.
acceptance_criteria: The service uses existing scrubbed bounded cancellable Git execution; disables replacement objects, external diff, textconv, and ambient rename changes; handles unmerged, sparse, gitlink, special, ignored, non-UTF-8, and rename-limit cases fail-closed; worktree includes staged, unstaged, and nonignored untracked content; copies never inherit debt; generic affected selection consumes the same comparison; the matcher primitive is independently tested while legacy epoch behavior remains unchanged until Task C.

title: Add durable native file-budget context, results, and contract epoch
description:
## Outcome

Extend the authored contract and immutable run plan so selected built-in file-budget targets carry authenticated policy and comparison preparation, typed native configuration, and exact execution authority; return typed bounded results with time-valid evidence.

## Boundary

Own optional lazy ComparisonRequestV1, PreparedNativeInputV1, independent policy/comparison preparation states, policy-first failure precedence, configured strict-inventory fallback, NativeFileBudgetConfigV1 and hard caps, NativeActionContext, NativeActionResult, finding totals/digests, exact-tree identities, run-plan compatibility, receipt valid-until propagation, and one serialized contract epoch. Own the epoch-gated target-local input switch over Task B and coordinate epoch allocation with argv-runner work.
acceptance_criteria: Untrusted plans replay-authenticate every policy, comparison, diagnostic, configuration, work-plan, requested-object, peeled-commit, and tree identity before acceptance; workers use persisted OIDs only; invalid policy becomes Failure, blocked comparison becomes Blocked, and configured fallback becomes ready strict inventory with original failure evidence; old plans and receipts remain readable; validity expires direct, batch, scoped, reusable, latest, and archival evidence; target-local non-empty inputs select only intended targets in the new epoch while legacy epochs retain component behavior.

title: Ship the native file-budget engine, CLI, and CI behavior
description:
## Outcome

Integrate the pure evaluator and durable native contract into repo:file-budget plus built-in check, audit, explain, and validate diagnostics with provider-neutral CI comparisons.

## Boundary

Own execution-time scope materialization, safe streaming measurement, pure-diagnostic to Finding mapping, direct human and versioned JSON output, exact selector grammar, direct-command defaults and hard-capped overrides, output/resource bounds, strict-inventory execution, push-before CI selection, and normalized conclusions. Repository action execution remains ordinary Jig orchestration; direct diagnostics create no run or receipt.
acceptance_criteria: Zero-selector checks use default-branch merge base with history and empty-tree UnbornWorktree authority without history; --base, --exact-tree, --staged, and --strict-inventory are unambiguous; direct config is independent of replaced or removed actions; matched arbitrary regular bytes are measured without binary heuristics or symlink following; resource exhaustion blocks; findings and evaluation digests are complete despite bounded previews; push CI uses exact before identity and unavailable nonzero history blocks unless checked-in fallback was prepared.

title: Seed repository policy and add crash-recoverable lifecycle migration
description:
## Outcome

Fresh and adopted repositories receive a seed-once authored .jig/file-budget.toml and replaceable repo:file-budget action; update and recopy preserve repository authority and migrate old generated Bash assets through a two-invocation proof protocol.

## Boundary

Own repository-model rule contributions, adoption preview, byte-preserved policy seeding outside managed replacement, action/alias/profile preservation, typed native config rendering, a full-update transaction, fsynced Git-metadata crash journal, transaction-owned rollback, foreign-write recovery, fresh-receipt proof, staged post-update identity comparison, and a durable legacy generation/digest table. Policy without action and custom replacement are legal.
acceptance_criteria: Phase one publishes seed policy and managed wiring through the crash-recoverable transaction while retaining Bash; phase two retires only exact generated assets after under-lock proof revalidation against the staged post-update authority; every uncommitted crash journal rolls back and never resumes retirement; committed journals only clean up; foreign bytes are preserved with recovery guidance; policy never enters managed replacement; human-required waiver authorization blocks mutation; post-deletion binaries retain downstream migration capability without embedding checker source.

title: Delete the temporary Bash checker after universal source dogfood
description:
## Outcome

Finish pull request #18 with the universal action proven by Jig source dogfood and no temporary Bash checker source, template, embedded snapshot, or Bash-specific test machinery.

## Boundary

Own deletion from this source branch only, replacement of Bash-specific tests with native policy/scope/contract/lifecycle coverage, final compatibility notes and stale-semantics searches. Downstream recognition and two-phase retirement remain Task E responsibilities and must work in a newly built post-deletion binary.
acceptance_criteria: The existing source-dogfood task has passed on the allocated authored contract epoch; all checker copies and Bash-only integration machinery are gone; source, templates, embedded assets, rendered fixtures, CI, release validation, aliases, and documentation use the universal action; old supported contracts remain readable without restoring Rust-native LOC dispatch; full test, format, Clippy, contract, rendered-repository, and file-budget gates pass on Linux and macOS.
